Subject: Sudden p99 jump — some requests 3-5s slower than usual (region: us-west)

Irene,

We're seeing a sharp regression in p99 latency against calls to your hosted text-generation endpoint for our prod traffic. Baseline p99 is ~430ms, but starting ~08:45 PDT we see a rolling set of requests at 2.8–4.6s. p95 is up too (from ~230ms to ~950ms). Error rates are low but throughput is degraded because clients are timing out and retrying.

This is impacting our recommender timeouts in checkout. Engineering asks whether this is on your side or ours — can you confirm if anything changed (deploy, config, warmup) or if you're seeing cache misses? We've attached a short log excerpt and a perf dashboard snapshot.

Attachments: vendera_error_log_snippet.txt (text), vendera_p99_snapshot.png (image)

We need an ETA for mitigation; our SRE will escalate if we don't get a workaround in the next 60m.

— Angela

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p99 jump — some requests 3-5s slower than usual (region: us-west)

Quick findings from infra triage:
- Correlated spike time: ~08:42–09:10 PDT.
- Root cause signal: a rolling prefix snapshot refresh job (part of our weekly snapshot compaction) accidentally restarted early for us-west; this cleared several prefix/KV caches and caused massive cold-KV lookup latency for hot prefixes used by Vendera.
- Evidence: elevated KV lookup RTs (median KV fetch 1.6ms -> 18ms for affected keys), prefix cache miss rate jumped from 2% -> 42% for a 22-minute window. Logs and metric links attached.

Immediate mitigations applied (10:00 PDT):
1) Paused the snapshot refresh job in us-west (stop-gap).
2) Triggered targeted KV warmup for Vendera prefixes (background parallel warmup to seeded instances).
3) Applied emergency routing policy: route Vendera's traffic to a warm Dedicated pool in us-west for 30m.

Next steps (owner):
- Dylan: monitor p95/p99; if metrics normalize in 15–30m we can keep the Dedicated route until a full warmup completes.
- Marcus: audit the snapshot scheduling and add a safety lock to avoid early restarts.
- Monica: confirm with Vendera that routing to Dedicated is acceptable and share rollback conditions.

Attachments: vendera_kv_metrics_08-42-09-10.log [attachment: vendera_error_log_snippet.txt]

I'll post metric links to the ticket INF-7890.

— Dylan (Oncall Infra)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Angela Kim <angela.kim@vendera.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: sudden p99 latency spike impacting Vendera — immediate update

Angela — quick update and apologies for the disruption.

What we found: a scheduled snapshot compaction job in us-west restarted early and cleared several prefix/KV caches, which produced a sharp transient rise in p95/p99 for hot prefixes used by Vendera. Dylan's team paused the job, ran targeted warmup for affected prefixes, and temporarily routed your traffic to a warm Dedicated pool.

Impact so far: p95 and p99 returned to within SLA thresholds by ~12:40 PDT after warmup and routing; we've left the Dedicated route in place while we add longer-term safeguards. We've attached a short SLO impact summary.

Planned follow-ups:
- Engineering will add a snapshot restart safety-lock and an early-warning metric for prefix-miss spikes (owner: Marcus).
- We'll publish a post-incident note and timeline into INF-7890 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7890).
- We'll provide Vendera with a short remediation playbook (how we will avoid this, and ops steps if it reoccurs).

Monica will follow up on credits/contract remediation if requested.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute bridge to walk your SREs through what happened.

Best — Irene
